logline: Decades later, the friends fill the white temple POET rebuilt. Between the laughing, the hugs and the football, he looks into the empty rooms of the dead and holds his glass of burning sand while it runs.
reading:
A reunion poem told as compressed time. 'Decades later' there is 'less time for words and more space for laughter, hugs with no reason, loud voices so our hearts can be overheard.' Joy is loud on purpose, so the heart can be heard. Its counter-images are short and dark: 'my mind drifts into the darkness of our afterlives, and those rooms are empty.' The gratitude is wide and specific, 'to every living tree in the forest for the shared years and the shared memories.'

It pivots on 'and those rooms are empty. We are all here, each holding our glasses of burning sands and known journeys'. The empty afterlife rooms turn into presence, and the toast glass becomes an hourglass on fire, so time runs out while they celebrate. 'This is brotherhood' (followed by the longest pause, 1.9 s) is the poem's answer. Its most physical image follows: 'we can place our ears upon the next brother's soul and follow paths of hilltops and canyons, of blinding lights and infinite nights', ending on 'laughter and football and recollections that bring us home every time.' The page text adds elders 'now past' and winds that 'part ways', which the spoken take leaves out; stage them lightly.
motifs: glasses of burning sand: toast and hourglass in one object
hearts overheard: sound leaving the chest
the empty rooms of the afterlives
an ear laid on the next brother's soul
the old photo restaged decades later
every living tree in the forest
football and recollections that bring us home
blinding lights and infinite nights: the shared road

light_and_texture: Warm low evening light inside a white hall, with practical glows (hourglass flames, the wall screen) doing most of the modelling and long soft shadows thrown by the cards onto the white walls. For the afterlife rooms everything drops to blue-black, and the elders are pale tracing-paper figures backlit so the paper grain glows. The archive photo is a real-feeling white-bordered card with a deckled edge and slight curl. Bodies are dense kraft card, and the hourglasses are clear acetate over painted sand so the flame reads through glass.

passage.keep: The hinge line ('and those rooms are empty. We are all here, each holding our glasses of burning sands') and the grip that closes and holds are right: one gesture, held. The window is a vertical pane, the strongest kind of surface. The NIH answer 'we're holding our own' is a quiet echo of 'holding our'.
passage.better: Make the grip a two-card replacement (cup → closed fist) so it closes in one beat, and add a head-lowered card at the same frame. The skyline window in view_042 sits at the far end of the hall and is small, so push in or re-stage beside a near side window, so the archive fills at least a third of the frame. Paint the hourglass large and bright (flame lit) so it reads at medium-wide. If the NIH clip is a talking head, it reads weakly; Coffee Break's hourglass (arch_7aa7b9d2) is a stronger literal answer to drop into the same window.
